# Earliest Finish Time for Land and Water Rides I.

@example Water ride 2 runs from 7 to 10, then land ride 1 from 10 to 12. Starting with a land ride ends at 13 at best.
[4,9]
[6,2]
[3,12,7]
[8,1,3]
=> 12

@example The land ride ends at 9; you wait for water ride 0 to open at 15 and get off at 17. Water ride 1 first, until 15, then the land ride, ends at 18.
[6]
[3]
[15,2]
[2,13]
=> 17

# The smallest values.
[1]
[1]
[1]
[1]
=> 3

# The largest values: the second ride starts at 2000.
[1000]
[1000]
[1000]
[1000]
=> 3000

# A land ride ends first (land ride 1 at 15, the water ride at 18), but
# going water first is better: water 11 to 18, then land ride 1 from 18 to
# 20. Land first ends at 22 at best.
[10,13]
[6,2]
[11]
[7]
=> 20

# After the land ride ends at 10, water ride 1 (alone it would end at 11)
# beats water ride 0 (alone it would end at 9): 12 against 18.
[4]
[6]
[1,9]
[8,2]
=> 12

# After the land ride ends at 11, the longer water ride 1 is better than
# the shorter one, which opens only at 50.
[1]
[10]
[50,3]
[1,5]
=> 16

# The land ride that opens first is the long one; the best first ride is
# land ride 1, ending at 3, and the water ride opens at 5.
[1,2]
[100,1]
[5]
[4]
=> 9

# The water ride opens exactly when the land ride ends: no wait.
[6]
[4]
[10]
[3]
=> 13

# Both water rides end before the land ride opens at 7, so you wait.
[7]
[2]
[2,5]
[3,1]
=> 9

# Three land rides, one water ride: the best land ride is the last one.
[30,20,10]
[2,1,5]
[12]
[2]
=> 17

# One land ride, three water rides: the best water ride is the last one.
[8]
[8]
[3,25,14]
[20,1,4]
=> 20

# Duplicate rides; both orders give 10.
[4,4]
[3,3]
[4,4]
[3,3]
=> 10

# The long water ride goes first; the land ride has been open for a while.
[500]
[1]
[1]
[1000]
=> 1002

[1,1]
[2,1]

[12,9]
[10,4]
[1,12]
=> 13
